You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Demo: a vertical 5-line at col 2, rows 2-5, with a horizontal pattern at row 5 (cols 3-9: 6 6 6 9 9 9). Output: the pattern is replicated across rows 2-5 (the extent of the vertical line), i.e., the pattern gets tiled/extended along the line's perpendicular... Actually the output: rows 2-5 each have cols 2-9 = 5 6 6 6 9 9 9. So the vertical line of 5s stays, and the pattern attached to its end is extended upward along the line.

In the test input: horizontal 5 line at row 1 (cols 0-4) and vertical 5 line col 6 (rows 1-8). Patterns attached: left column has colors 4,2,2,2,2,1 at rows 2-6 (attached below the horizontal line at col 0), and bottom-right pattern 8 6 8 / 3 3 3 at rows 7-8, cols 7-9 (attached to vertical line's end at row 8, cols 7-9).

Alternatively, pattern aligns so its bottom row is at line end and repeats the pattern vertically tiling.

What about the horizontal 5 line at row 1 with the left column pattern (rows 2-6, col 0: 4,2,2,2,2,1)? That pattern is attached below the horizontal line at its left end. Extend rightward along row 1? Line spans cols 0-4, pattern is 5 rows tall (rows 2-6), 1 wide. Extend: replicate the column pattern across columns 0-4: each column c in 0-4 gets the same vertical pattern rows 2-6? That would give 5x5 block: cols 0-4, rows 2-6, each column = [4,2,2,2,2,1] rows 2-6 → column values rows2..6: 4,2,2,2,1 (5 rows: rows 2,3,4,5,6 → colors 4,2,2,2,1).

Similarly vertical line col 6 rows 1-8 with 2-row pattern at rows 7-8 cols 7-9: replicate pattern horizontally? No — demo: pattern attached at end of line extends along the line direction. Demo line was vertical, pattern horizontal at its bottom, extended upward (along the line). And vertical line col 6, pattern at bottom, 2-row 3-wide, extend upward along line: replicate the 2-row block upward for rows 1-8. Rows 1-8 is 8 rows, block is 2 rows: tiling from bottom: rows 7-8, 5-6, 3-4, 1-2.

But wait — do these overlap? Cols 0-4 rows 2-6 and cols 7-9 rows 1-8. No overlap with col 6 (line stays). Row 1: cols 0-4 are the 5 line already, cols 7-9 get pattern from rows 1-2 (block row 1 = 8 6 8? or 3 3 3?).

Tiling upward: pattern block rows (top=8 6 8, bottom=3 3 3). Rows 7-8 = block as-is. Row 6 = bottom row (3 3 3)? If tiling periodically with period 2 aligned at bottom: row r gets pattern[(r-7) mod 2]: row7=idx0 (8 6 8), row8=idx1 (3 3 3), row6 = idx -1 mod 2 = idx1 = 3 3 3, row5 = idx0, row4 = idx1, row3=idx0, row2=idx1, row1=idx0.

Test: vertical line col 6, rows 1-8; pattern cols 7-9 (perpendicular extent), rows 7-8. Fill rows 1-8 × cols 7-9, repeating pattern along rows: same as computed above.

Wait, but the pattern attached below line starting at row 2... line row 1, pattern begins row 2 directly below. Test horizontal line: row 1, cols 0-4, pattern col 0, rows 2-6. Fill rows 2-6, cols 0-4 with column pattern repeated across cols 0-4.

Row 1: cols 0-4 = 5 (line), col 6 = 5, cols 7-9 = pattern row1 (8 6 8) if tiling gives idx0 at row1. Hmm rows 1-8 with period 2 aligned bottom: row1=8 6 8, row2=3 3 3, row3=8 6 8, row4=3 3 3, row5=8 6 8, row6=3 3 3, row7=8 6 8, row8=3 3 3.

Confidence moderate. Alternative: extend could flip/alternate. Also possible that the pattern extends along the line only up to where line length allows with same orientation (not tiling but sliding?). I'll go with periodic tiling.

Actually another interpretation: pattern extended such that each row gets a copy — in demo with 1-row pattern, rows 2-5 all identical. With 2-row pattern, maybe each of rows 1-8 gets the full 2-row block repeated? No, that breaks dimension. Periodic tiling is most natural. Submit.
